findings.proposed_severity: Minor: the printed homotopy-sheaf index is false, but the local replacement and divisibility argument restore the stated lemma without altering the main theorem
findings.location: Lemma 4.0.7, the displayed identification after 'We know from Corollary 3.0.2 that', printed PDF page 35
findings.exact_issue: pi_{d+1}^A1(A^{d+2} minus 0) is identified with K_{d+1}^MW and then K_{d+1}^M. The correct weight in both places is d+2.
verification: The paper's own first-homotopy-sheaf formula on page 14 says pi_{n-1}(A^n minus 0)=K_n^MW. Substitute n=d+2.
The fiber sequence immediately above the erroneous line really uses A^{d+2} minus 0; the problem is not an extraction error or a different index convention.
The relevant image on page 35 was actually displayed and inspected.
complete_local_repair: Replace K_{d+1}^MW and K_{d+1}^M in that line with K_{d+2}^MW and K_{d+2}^M. The reduction from Milnor-Witt to Milnor K-theory is valid on X by the vanishing of the relevant I-power.

The last Rost-Schmid term for H^d(X,K_{d+2}^M) is the direct sum of K_2^M(k) over closed points. For any positive integer N and any Milnor symbol {a,b}, choose c in k with c^N=a. Then {a,b}=N{c,b}. Hence K_2^M(k), the direct sum, and its top-cohomology quotient are N-divisible.
Lemma 2.4.1 with sphere dimension d+2 and m=d+1 shows that the cokernel of H^d pi_{d+1}(GL_{d+2})->H^d pi_{d+1}(A^{d+2} minus 0) is annihilated by (d+1)!.
This cokernel is H^d of the image sheaf called A in the proof, by cohomological dimension. It is both (d+1)!-divisible and annihilated by (d+1)!, so it is zero.
The second short exact sequence then yields the claimed stabilization isomorphism. No uniqueness of the divisibility or additional exclusion of characteristic d+1 is needed for this repair.
findings.impact_limit: This is a local incorrect displayed formula. It does not establish a counterexample to Lemma 4.0.7, the cohomology vanishing theorem, or cancellation.

main_range_completion.title: Completing the cohomology-kernel inference in Lemma 4.0.8 under the main theorem's hypotheses
assumptions: X is smooth affine of dimension d>=4 over algebraically closed k.
N=d! is invertible in k. This is the main cancellation theorem's characteristic restriction.
Use the paper's cited norm-residue, Rost-Schmid, contraction, and Suslin-map inputs. No author code is involved.
notation: The long exact homotopy sequence gives D->E --r--> A; the preceding cokernel B injects into D. The Milnor-Witt sheaf at this spot equals A on X by the I-power vanishing.
There is a Suslin-induced map t:A->E with r t=N id_A. This follows from the coordinate-power relation with sphere dimension d+1, homotopy degree d, and sqrt(-1) in k.

steps.statement: A is N-divisible as a sheaf on the small Nisnevich site of X.
steps.proof: For each prime ell dividing N, ell differs from char(k). Every generic field of a scheme etale over X has transcendence degree at most d over algebraically closed k, so its ell-cohomological dimension is at most d. Norm residue gives K_{d+1}^M(F)/ell=H_et^{d+1}(F,mu_ell^{tensor(d+1)})=0. The strictly A1-invariant quotient sheaf K_{d+1}^M/ell is unramified and therefore vanishes on these schemes when its generic values vanish. Thus A/ell=0, and multiplying the prime factors gives N-divisibility.

Each closed point x is k-rational and lies on an integral affine curve C in X. Normalize C; its normalization is a smooth affine curve, finite over C, with a k-point above x. For a smooth affine curve over an algebraically closed field, Pic is divisible: embed it in a smooth projective curve, use a boundary k-point to remove the degree part, and use divisibility of the k-points of the Jacobian. Pushforward of an N-root of the point class from the normalized curve gives an N-root of [x] in CH_0(X). Closed points generate CH_0, so the entire group is divisible.

steps.statement: H^d(X, _ell A)=0 for every prime ell dividing N.
steps.proof: Contraction of the ell-torsion sheaf is exact in the strictly A1-invariant category. The final Rost-Schmid term for _ell A is the sum of _ell K_1^M(k)=mu_ell(k) over the closed points. Choose a primitive root tau to identify each summand with Z/ell. In codimension d-1, the torsion symbols {tau,f} in _ell K_2^M(k(C)) have residues tau^{ord_z(f)} (up to the consistent boundary convention). Their boundaries include the principal-divisor relations modulo ell. Consequently the top cohomology is a quotient of CH_0(X)/ell, which is zero by Step 2.

Step 1 makes 0->_ell A->A --ell-->A->0 a short exact sequence on X. Its long exact cohomology sequence and Step 3 make multiplication by ell onto on H^{d-1}(X,A). Apply this successively to the prime factors of N.

steps.statement: Both r:E->A and H^{d-1}(r) are onto.
steps.proof: For a local section a of A, choose an N-root b by Step 1, and r(t(b))=a. For a cohomology class alpha in H^{d-1}(A), choose an N-root beta by Step 4 and use H^{d-1}(t)(beta). The composite on cohomology is multiplication by N.

steps.statement: The desired cohomology kernel is the image of H^d(B).
steps.proof: Set J=ker(r)=im(D->E). From 0->J->E->A->0, the surjectivity of H^{d-1}(r) implies that H^d(J)->H^d(E) is injective. From 0->B->D->J->0, cohomological dimension at most d gives exact H^d(B)->H^d(D)->H^d(J)->0. Combining these sequences proves ker[H^d(D)->H^d(E)]=im[H^d(B)->H^d(D)].

steps.statement: That kernel is annihilated by N=d!.
steps.proof: The preceding homotopy segment gives pi_{d+1}(GL_{d+1})->pi_{d+1}(A^{d+1} minus 0)->B->0. Top cohomology is right exact here. Lemma 2.4.1, with sphere dimension d+1 and homotopy degree d+1, makes its cohomology cokernel N-torsion. This cokernel is H^d(B), so Step 6 gives the required bound.

main_range_completion.range_check: For the last Suslin bound, 2<=d+1<=2(d+1)-4 holds when d>=3. For r t=N id at degree d, the range holds when d>=2. The actual use here is d>=4.
main_range_completion.limitation: This is a proof completion under N invertible. It is not a claimed proof of the broader char(k)!=2 lemma when char(k) divides N; that case would require additional characteristic-p input or another argument.

proof_completeness_observations.remaining: This review does not complete characteristic dividing d! under only characteristic!=2. No counterexample claimed.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed one-step weight error with a complete local repair.
per_problem.reasoning: The source's own formula pi_(n-1)(A^n minus 0)=K_n^MW gives weight d+2 at pi_(d+1)(A^(d+2) minus 0). The p.35 fibre sequence really uses A^(d+2), so the printed weight d+1 is not an extraction or convention issue. Corollary 3.0.2 changes MW to Milnor on X at the corrected weight.
per_problem.repair: The last Gersten term for H^d(K_(d+2)^M) is a direct sum of K2^M(k). Algebraic closedness gives a=c^N and {a,b}=N{c,b}, for every N including N divisible by the characteristic. Thus the group and its cohomology quotient are divisible, without asserting injectivity of multiplication. Lemma 2.4.1 at sphere dimension d+2 and homotopy degree d+1 annihilates the cokernel by (d+1)!. Right exactness of top cohomology then makes that cokernel both divisible and bounded-torsion, hence zero. The second short exact sequence yields the stated stabilization isomorphism. No extra exclusion of characteristic d+1 is needed.
per_problem.impact: The incorrect displayed identification is real, but the lemma and cancellation conclusion are not refuted; Minor is supported.

per_problem.severity: Proof-completeness observation; wider characteristic range remains Needs Evidence
per_problem.source: PDF pp.17,20,35-36 and the existing report's explicit image-sheaf comparison
per_problem.verdict: The added argument is valid in the main theorem's d!-invertible range; it does not establish the entire wider auxiliary range.
per_problem.reasoning: An exact sheaf segment B->D->E alone cannot identify ker H^d(D)->H^d(E). With A=K_(d+1)^M|X, N=d!, the Suslin map gives r:E->A and t:A->E with rt=N id, in the stated stable range. For ell|N and ell different from char(k), generic etale fields have cohomological dimension <=d; norm residue and unramifiedness give A/ell=0. The last Rost-Schmid term of _ell A is a sum of mu_ell(k). Torsion symbols {tau,f} have tame residues tau^ord(f), so boundaries contain principal-divisor relations modulo ell. This yields CH0(X)/ell onto H^d(_ell A). Every point lies on an integral affine curve; finite normalization and the divisible Picard group of the smooth affine curve give divisibility of CH0(X). Therefore H^d(_ell A)=0, and the short exact multiplication-by-ell sequence makes H^(d-1)(A) ell-divisible. Iterating factors of N makes r and H^(d-1)(r) surjective.
per_problem.kernel_check: For J=ker r=im(D->E), the first short exact sequence 0->J->E->A->0 now makes H^d(J)->H^d(E) injective. The second 0->B->D->J->0 gives the desired kernel as the image of H^d(B). The previous homotopy segment and Lemma 2.4.1 make this image N-torsion. Both range inequalities for degree d and d+1 at sphere dimension d+1 hold in the running d>=4 setting.
per_problem.counterevidence_and_limit: No false lemma or counterexample has been established by the omitted justification alone. Norm residue/cohomological dimension here require ell prime to characteristic. Thus the completion covers the main d!-invertible theorem, but not Lemma 4.0.8/Proposition 4.0.9 in all characteristics different from two when char(k) divides d!. Keeping that remainder as Needs Evidence is correct.
